column1: # SANSOS RV64GC mnemonic registry — task B-001, doc 02 §2.3.
# Rule R-02-1: every architectural instruction has a Sassembly name. There is no
# `.insn 0x…` escape hatch, so an instruction absent from this file cannot be
# written at all — which is the point: the ISA surface is finite and reviewed.
# Rule R-02-2: names are PER FAMILY, not per encoding. `योगः` covers add, addi,
# addw and addiw; the assembler picks the encoding from the operand kinds and the
# sizing suffix (व्याप्ति: .अ८ .अ१६ .अ३२ .अ६४, default .अ६४). That is why ~193
# architectural instructions need far fewer names — the compressed C extension
# adds no names at all, since c.add IS योगः and the assembler emits the short
# `source` is `lexicon` when spec/lexicon.tsv already names the concept, and
# `coined` when this file introduces it. Coined terms must be added to
# lexicon.src.tsv before B-002 freezes the grammar — doc 01 §4 rule 5 is one
# word, one sense, and a mnemonic that exists only here is a second vocabulary.
# `encoding` is DELIBERATELY EMPTY. B-008 fills it from the pinned specification
# PDF in research/specs/isa/. A half-remembered opcode that looks authoritative
# is worse than a blank, and this file is where that temptation lives.
# Columns: family, devanagari, gloss, ext, covers, encoding, source

column1: # The first privileged instruction in this registry. Everything above it is
# usable in any mode; this one is the kernel's, and paging cannot be turned on
# without it — a satp write that is not followed by a fence leaves the old
# translations live, and a machine that caches them goes on running against the
# `sret` leaves a trap. `C-001d1` proved a handler can be REACHED; without this
# it can only shut the machine down, because there is no way back to the
# instruction after the one that trapped.
# The name is not coined. `विघ्नप्रत्यागमः` — return from interrupt — is already
# in the lexicon, already categorised `mnemonic`, and was unused: doc 01 §4 is
# one word one sense, so inventing a second name for a sense the lexicon had
# already settled would be the error, not the economy.
